This walks that thin line between 'random' and 'unexplained' really, really well. I think it's all the small hooks and the loose thematic cohesion that make it work - the wet paint, the egyptian amulet, that indian dude in general, the seats in the cockpit being made from computer parts…

There's a ton of angles to come at this from for Wild Mass Guessing, which is ultimately what makes this one so damn fun.

A hearty +1 from me!

item.content:encoded: Thank you. The wet paint, that dried like it was regular paint, is the most goosebumpy thing in this SCP. Do you know just how many man hours go into painting that many square feet? About 200 man hours, if done by professional painters. With a maximum of 30 minutes before being dry to the touch, that means a minimum of 400 people in order to finish painting the plane evenly. Otherwise the paint is itself anomalous. Sometimes watching paint dry isn't boring, sometimes it breaks your brain.

item.content:encoded:
I didn't get lol-random off of this the way I have with some articles on the site. The events feel tied together, but with a logic that is utterly incomprehensible. That made it substantially more creepy to me than a lot of the more coherent narrative articles that I've read so far. The feeling that there was something just on the edge of making sense, that maybe I could actually understand it if I could just get a tiny bit more information, but that I might not actually want to know. It's almost as if the anomaly was the result of actions by some being so alien that there was simply no mutual frame of reference where some sort of understanding could be achieved.

That kind of thing is hard to do effectively, and this article definitely earned an upvote for that.

item.content:encoded: Overall, I enjoyed this. I think of it as a perfect example of what the Foundation might look to contain. This is potentially dangerous to the common person, has little to no discernible explanation and can be kept sequestered away with little to no risk. If any explanation were to be gathered from this giant flying metal tube of confusion, it's likely explain a lot. There is always the concern of lolrandom but I think that's appreciated and acknowledged here. It just fits its niche in the cannon ever so nicely.

This was interesting. Not a particularly scary or harmful SCP, or one with a complex backstory, but the random slightly creepy paranormal effects picture perfectly the "what the heck" feeling the description of a plane painted all blue and full of decayed stuff and bodies of living people brings up.

I do believe a supplemental event log would do it even more good, though, we don't have a lot to go on. The little there is at the moment is good, but as with other high-scoring SCPs, one can never have too much as long as long as quality standards are observed.

Also, yay for pancakes!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Long shot, but here's my best guess:

The amulet on the Indian man in the waste compartment is the root cause of the June 1987 anomaly. Somehow, it allows (or at least allowed) its carrier to manipulate space-time in four dimensions. There is loose thematic ground for this, as the Wadjet Eye in ancient Egypt represented a direct connection to the forces responsible for creating and shaping the universe. This man, working as a hitman for organized crime in California, used (rather, will use, as this must take place at some point in the future) the amulet to facilitate accurate travel and escape via the use of warping space to create wormholes.

At some point, this man was hired to kill someone on board a plane, mid-flight. Instead of stowing away on the plane, he attempted to use the amulet to "warp" aboard the flight mid-air. However, at the same time he attempted to create a wormhole, the flight was rocked by turbulence, and the point of arrival was moved into the waste compartment. Panicking, he attempted to immediately create a second wormhole to escape the compartment, which resulted in a massive spatial anomaly which engulfed the entire airplane, sucking it into a wormhole.

Because it was incomplete, the other end of the hole closed before the transit was finished, and the plane experienced a temporal collapse, compressing all time that would have been experienced by objects within the plane into an instant. This had the immediate effect of replacing all humans on board with their corpses at the time of their deaths from various point in the "future." In addition, as the plane was now outside the known universe, reality contained within the plane began to decay, with numerous bizarre results detailed in the article.

After some "time," the plane reentered the known universe, manifesting itself in what we would call its "past" at its resting place in Washington State in June, 1987. Reality within the craft remains permanently altered and occasional anomalous breaches reflect this, which is why it violently repels fully "real" sentient observers for a time period following these events; perhaps the corrupted reality fundamentally repels the normal version as a defense mechanism against creating a paradox.

I'm sure the physics are BS, and it doesn't explain everything, but this could be a reasonable hypothesis for explaining:

  • Why there was a guy in the waste compartment
  • Why he had a shotgun
  • Why he had an odd Egyptian pendant
  • Why everyone on board is dead in a seemingly unrelated variety of ways
  • Why, in general, events that take place on board are bizarre but consistently composed of recognizable elements
  • Why people are repelled for a time period following an event on the airplane
  • Why the optometrist from Georgia claims never to have been on a plane, as his plane ride takes place at some point in the future

Upvoted, by the way.

item.content:encoded:
The plane is the manifestation of the inner rage of Seymour Fitzgerald, specifically the rage against those around him. The victims of the plane are all the people who have at some point pissed this guy off to the point of wishing them dead (or at least mutilated). Seymour, as it were, has a bit of a short fuse, so a lot of people tend to make him angry. For instance, he's never met the optometrist from Atlanta, Georgia. In fact, Seymour has never even been to Atlanta, Georgia. But ███████ ██████████ was driving to his daughter's house in Birmingham, Alabama when he happened to accidentally cut off another driver when he merged into the left lane on the interstate.

Seymour doesn't like bad drivers, you know, especially ones who cut him off.

The anomalous events within the plane are various things that have happened to Seymour during his life. For example, on January 1st, 2001, Seymour was taken to the hospital after his appendix burst. The poor fellow had an extraordinarily high fever, causing him to drift in and out of delirium. In fact, at one point, he could have sworn he was on the cockpit of a plane, but a swift and brutal bout of vomiting snapped him out of it.

Back to the meat of the issue, though, Seymour is a very judgmental person. Whenever he gets mad at someone, he always some variation of the same thing: "One day that asshole will know what it means to be sorry!"

—

Yeah that kind of sucked.

Anyway, love the rewrite. Everything that made the original intriguing has been upped at least fivefold, and I for one am a fan. +1.
